name: oxo-flow-eager
title: Ancient DNA (aDNA): QC, mapping, damage estimation and genotyping
excluded: convertBam (ported as `convert_bam` but a documented dead end: with `bam_input=true && run_convertinputbam=true` the rule extracts FASTQ while downstream still runs on the fixture FASTQs — upstream wires convertBam into the preprocessing channels; wiring it needs optional-input semantics, Traitome/oxo-flow#200; see the README fidelity row)
not_applicable: output_documentation: nf-core boilerplate docs process (markdown_to_html.py of static run docs); upstream runs it unconditionally, so porting it would change the default plan for zero analytical value
get_software_versions: nf-core boilerplate versions process (scrapes $workflow/$nextflow native variables into a versions.yml, which has no oxo-flow equivalent)

library_merge / additional_library_merge: the port's data model has ONE library per sample (directory input, library = sample, lane = 0) and one BAM per sample at every stage, so there are no per-LIBRARY dedup/bam_trim BAMs to merge (upstream merges them per sample, main.nf 1967 / 2320). Model-checked 2026-09-07 against oxo-flow 0.17.2 with a 4-probe feasibility study (/tmp/libmerge-probe): (1) an undeclared {library} wildcard in an output pattern stays literal and fails at run time ('contains unbound wildcard {library} ... declare a value source'); (2) [[values]] library fan-out produces the per-library BAMs, but expand_inputs over a {library}-dimension pattern re-fans the MERGE per library value (one instance per value all writing the same output — last-writer-wins, not a per-sample gather); (3) input_groups pattern = 'results/dedup/*/{sample}_*_rmdup.bam' with group_by = 'sample' DOES fold per-library files S1_LIB1/S1_LIB2 into one S1 group (probe4, verified end-to-end: one library_merge instance per sample, {input} = both BAMs, {input_group.library} = 'LIB1 LIB2') — so a per-sample samtools merge is expressible, BUT only after re-keying the entire eager chain per {sample}_{library}: upstream runs every step (adapter removal, mapping, dedup) per library and merges the BAMs at the end, while the port keys everything by {sample} alone. That is a sizable model change (issue #20's own framing) affecting every rule, not a targeted port of 3 merge rules. Declaring each library as its own sample (or pre-merging lanes/libraries upstream of the port) remains the practical workaround

seqtype_merge: upstream merges the per-seqtype mapped BAMs of mixed PE/SE libraries into one BAM per library (samtools merge, main.nf 1597); the port is pure-PE (directory input, sample = text before _R1/_R2) with one mapped BAM per sample, so there are no mixed-PE/SE BAMs to merge. Convert SE samples to PE or run SE-only samples separately
description: Ancient DNA (aDNA) analysis in one run: FastQC raw QC, optional fastp poly-G filtering (2-colour chemistry), AdapterRemoval adapter clipping and paired-end read merging, BWA aln mapping with ancient-DNA parameters, picard MarkDuplicates (or DeDup) deduplication, preseq library-complexity curves, DamageProfiler damage estimation, Qualimap BAM QC, optional pileupCaller genotyping with eigenstrat SNP coverage, optional metagenomic screening of the unmapped reads (bbduk entropy complexity filter, MALT or kraken2 classification with kraken_parse/kraken_merge tables, MaltExtract aDNA evaluation), and a final MultiQC report — every rule pinned to the nf-core/eager 2.5.3 tool versions in the upstream container (MALT 0.61 and HOPs 0.35 ship in the pinned nfcore/eager:2.5.3 image).

installation.engine: oxo-flow >= 0.12.0 (the gated multi-lane mode — run_lanemerge=true — additionally requires oxo-flow >= 0.16.0 with input_groups support, Traitome/oxo-flow#231; on older engines the gate is inert and the default single-pair path is unchanged)
installation.toolchain: containers (Docker/Singularity) — pinned image nfcore/eager:2.5.3 for all rules (bundles the pinned conda env from envs/eager.yaml)
requirements: reference genome FASTA, plain and uncompressed (.gz references are not supported — upstream's unzip_reference step is not ported); the workflow builds the .fai / .dict / BWA indices itself
paired-end FASTQ pairs named <sample>_R1.fastq.gz / <sample>_R2.fastq.gz in a directory (directory input mode; sample = text before the _R1/_R2 suffix); single-end is not supported

optional — BAM input: set bam_input=true and input_bam=<path to one BAM>. Default is the BAM pass-through: indexinputbam copies the BAM to results/mapping/bwa/<sample>_PE.mapped.bam (+ .bai, samtools index -c when large_ref=true) and the whole downstream BAM chain (flagstat, dedup, preseq, ...) consumes it unchanged. Alternatively run_convertinputbam=true routes through convert_bam, which extracts a paired-end FASTQ pair (results/convert_bam/<sample>_R{1,2}.fastq.gz, via samtools collate | samtools fastq -1/-2) that feeds FastQC (fastqc_baminput), fastp (when the poly-G gate is on) and AdapterRemoval in place of the raw fixture pair. Note {config.input_bam} is ONE path used per sample of the cohort — point it at a per-sample BAM or run one sample at a time. Unmapped-only BAMs (no @SQ lines) work; mapped BAMs are handled the same way

optional — multi-lane input: name the pairs <sample>_L<lane>_R1.fastq.gz / _R2.fastq.gz (lane-tagged, as in upstream's TSV mode) and set run_lanemerge=true: the lanemerge rules concatenate the per-lane pairs of each sample into one merged pair (results/lanemerging/) that feeds AdapterRemoval and hostremoval_input_fastq; samples without lane-tagged files keep using the default-named pair. Requires oxo-flow >= 0.16.0 (input_groups, Traitome/oxo-flow#231)

multi-library samples: upstream eager runs the whole chain per LIBRARY and merges the per-library BAMs at the end (library_merge / additional_library_merge). The port keys everything by sample (ONE library per sample); to analyse multiple libraries of one sample, declare each library as its own sample (e.g. S1_LIB1, S1_LIB2) or pre-merge the per-library FASTQs/BAMs upstream of the port. A per-sample merge after per-library processing was model-checked against oxo-flow 0.17.2 (2026-09-07) and would require re-keying the whole chain per {sample}_{library} — a sizable model change, see the metadata not_applicable entry for the probe evidence
optional — pileupCaller genotyping (run_genotyping=true genotyping_tool='pileupcaller') requires pileupcaller_snpfile and pileupcaller_bedfile; the rule fails fast without them

optional — metagenomic screening (run_metagenomic_screening=true, bam_unmapped_type='fastq') requires metagenomic_tool='kraken' with a kraken2_db (kraken2 database directory or .tar.gz bundle, unpacked by the kraken rule) or metagenomic_tool='malt' with a malt_db (MALT database directory); maltextract additionally requires maltextract_taxon_list and maltextract_ncbifiles. The chain is validate/dry-run-tested but not yet live-verified

compute: up to 4 CPUs / 8 GB RAM per rule (bwa_aln: 4 threads / 8G; kraken: 4 threads / 8G — upstream's mc_huge label is 32 cpus / 256 GB, tune via CLI overrides; reference-index and MultiQC rules up to 8 GB; base default 1 CPU / 7 GB / 24 h)
Docker or Singularity to run the pinned container nfcore/eager:2.5.3 (not needed for validate / lint / dry-run)
disk: results/ holds reference indices, mapped BAMs and reports — size grows with the reference genome and number of samples
